content: An ant! The ant sat on Sam. 'An ant! An ant!' The ant sat on Nat. 'An ant, Nat!' Sam and Nat sat. The ant sat and sat. Dad is in. The ant sat on Dad!

Dot the cat did not nap. 'Nap on the cot, Dot,' said Sam. Dot did not. Dot sat on Sam — and Dot did nap! Sam can not sip at a cup. Sam can not stand. A kid is in. 'Can I pat Dot?' said the kid. Pat, pat. Dot did not stop the nap. A cat is a cat!

Gus the pug dug and dug in the mud. A big fat nut! But a bug sat on the nut. 'A bug nut,' said the bug. 'A pug nut,' said Gus. Tug, tug, tug! Snap! Gus got a bit, and the bug got a bit. A hen is at the mud. The hen naps on the nut bed!

Ken has a hen. The hen is Hap. At sun up, Hap is not in the hut! 'Hap? Hap?' Ken hunts in the pen. He hunts at the mud pit. Not a hen. At the end, Ken can see a hen snug in the mint bed. Hap! 'Hap!' said Ken. He pats Hap. A red hen runs in — Hap's mom! Ken hugs his hens, and his hens nap in the sun.

Sal the rat sat in the log. Sal felt sad. 'I am a rat. Not a pal in the land.' A lad sat at the log. The lad had a book. Sal ran up and got on the lap of the lad. The lad let Sal look. The rat and the lad look at the book as the sun sets. Sal has a pal! And a pup runs up from the pond. The pup is wet — and it wags at Sal.

Max the fox got in a big box. But the box tips. Bam! The box is on Max. Max can not get up. 'Help! Help!' Jen ran to the box. Jen tugs and tugs. At last the box tips, and Max hops up. 'You did it, Jen!' Max zips off. Max and Jen jog up a hill. 'You are quick, Max,' said Jen. 'What a fox you are!'

Sam and Dad went to camp. Sam put up the tent. But the wind got bad, and Sam felt the cold wind on his hands. 'I can not get the tent up!' The tent flaps and flips. Dad grips the tent, and Sam pegs it. At last the tent stands. Sam and Dad sit snug in it: hot milk, nuts and a lamp. The wind went on and on, but Sam slept, glad and snug. What a camp!

The frog and the crab are best pals, but the frog brags. 'I can jump the best!' 'And I can dig the best,' said the crab. 'Let us test it!' The frog jumps and jumps. The crab digs and digs. The frog lands in the crab's pit! Plop! Sand on the frog. Sand on the crab. The pals grin. 'You win,' said the frog. 'And you win,' said the crab. The pals play in the sun until sunset. What a day!

A hen sat on a nest in the pen. The hen did not get up. Not at sun up. Not in the wind. Not at sunset. The hen kept the eggs safe. The eggs did not drop. At last — tap, tap, tap! Chicks! Wet chicks in the nest. The sun is hot, and the chicks get soft. The chicks nod and nap, snug in the nest. And the hen? The hen naps at last!

Sam got a drum. Bam! Bam! Bam! 'Stop!' said Mom. Sam did not stop. Bam! Bam! 'Stop!' said Dad. Sam did not stop. Mom got a plan. 'Sam, help us. The plums!' Sam ran to help. Mom and Sam got milk and plums. Dad set the plums and milk up. Sam sat and had a plum. It was fun to play the drum, but — yum! Plums win!

Bill fell in the mud. Splat! Mud on his legs. Mud on his hands. Mud up to his ribs! Dad ran to help. 'A mess!' said Dad. Dad got a wet rag and rubs and rubs. The mud gets off at last. But Bill sniffs. 'Dad — a sock is still in the mud!' Dad tugs it up. The sock is a big wet mess. Bill and Dad grin. Off to the tub, Bill!

Jill set the doll on the tall wall. 'Sit still, doll.' But the doll fell! Jill ran to tell Mom. 'The doll fell off the wall!' Mom got the doll. 'It is not a bad fall. The doll is full of fluff!' Jill hugs the doll. Jill and the doll roll a ball in the hall. At last Mom taps the tall clock in the hall. 'Bed, Jill!' Jill and the doll nod off. All is well.

Rick has a black cat, Jack. A big sack sat on the deck. Jack taps it. Click, clack! 'What is in the sack?' said Rick. Rick tips it up — and a tin ship lands on the deck! 'A ship!' said Rick. Rick sets the ship up on a box. And Jack? Jack gets in the sack and naps. What luck: Rick gets a ship, and Jack gets a sack!

Trish has a wish: a pet fish. 'A fish, Mom! A fish!' Mom and Trish shop and shop. At the pet shop, Trish picks a red fish. Swish, swish! The fish swims in a big glass dish. Trish sits still. 'Hush,' said Trish. 'The fish naps.' Mom grins. That fish is fun to watch!

'Get on this bus,' said Mom. 'That bus is full.' The big bus sets off. Ben sits at the back. Then the bus stops. And stops. And stops. 'Is that the mall?' 'Not yet, Ben.' The bus huffs on. At last — 'The mall!' Ben and Mom hop off, and off they dash. Ben runs in with Mom. Fun at the mall at last!

This is Seth. That is Beth. The pals met at the path. 'The hill!' said Seth. 'Up we go!' Up the path went the pals. The sun is hot. The wind huffs past them. Seth spots moths. Beth spots a thin bug. Up and up and up... at last, the top! The land is vast. 'This is the best,' said Beth. The pals sit and chat as the sun sets. Then Seth and Beth dash back, glad as can be.

Chuck is a chick. Chuck chomps and chomps. Chips! Chomp. Buns! Chomp. 'Chuck! Such chomps!' said Mom. 'Munch this fresh mash.' 'Not mash!' said Chuck. But Chuck had a bit. Munch. Munch, munch! 'This mash is not bad,' said Chuck. Chomp, chomp, chomp! When not a bit is left, Chuck naps in the sun, fat and glad.

Phil and Steph check the class graph. 'What is this graph of?' said Phil. 'Pets,' said Steph. 'Cats, dogs and fish. Which pet wins?' Phil checks. Lots of cats. Lots of dogs. Not lots of fish. 'The cats win!' 'When can we do the dog graph?' said Steph. The pals grin, and Phil hums a song.

The king can sing. And sing. And sing. His songs are long and strong. Bang went the gong along with him. The king's dog hid. The king's cat left. Still the king sang. At last a big pink van at the wall did a long honk: HONK! The king got the hint. 'Not a fan of songs?' The king quit. And all the land had a long, still rest.

Beth and Chuck pack a lunch: fresh rolls, chips and a jug of punch. Off to the pond! The wind sings in the long grass. Fish splash. A duck quacks at them. Beth and Chuck munch and munch. 'I wish I had a cake,' said Beth. 'A cake?' said Chuck. 'We can make it!' Back at the ranch, Mom helps them mix it up. What a lunch. What a cake!

Sam made a cake for Kate. Jam in it. Jam on it. Jam on Sam! Kate came in. 'A cake! For me?' Sam and Kate ate the cake in the shade. Not a bit was left. 'We ate it just in time,' said Kate. Then a game of tag in the shade. Tag! At the gate Kate gave Sam a big wave. 'Same game next time?' 'Yes!' said Sam.

Mike likes his red bike. Deb has five bikes, but likes the white bike best. Ride, ride, ride! The kids ride on the path in a line. Deb can ride with no hands! 'To the gate?' 'To the gate!' Zip, zip — side by side they ride, and Deb wins by a bit. Then Mike and Deb ride home in a line. What a fine ride!

Cole rode his bike home. At the gate, Cole stops. 'My note! I left my note on the stone step!' A rose is at the gate. A red bug sits on the rose. But the note? Cole hopes and hopes. Yes! The note is safe on the stone step. The note has his name on it — a note from Mom: 'I am glad you are my Cole.' Cole smiles and takes the note inside. His cute pup tags along.

June has a flute. She makes fine notes on it, but not yet a tune. Note upon note upon note... at last the notes line up: a tune! The mule likes it. The mule taps in time. Dave brings June a cup of ice. 'What a cute tune,' said Dave. 'And what a cute mule!' The mule nods. June grins and makes one last tune at home.

Lance and I race on the ice. I race past the mice twice! We slide and spin. My face is like ice, but the race is fun. Then Lance stops. 'What is that?' A stone shines in the ice. We scrape at the ice. The stone is huge! It shines in the sun. We take the huge stone to a safe place. A prize from the ice! What a race. What a place!

Jane is on the stage. She sang from a huge page of songs: a song of a cage, a song of a sage, a song of a big rage. Jane's face went red at the last page, but she sang on. The class claps and claps! Jane grins and hugs the page. 'The stage is the place for me!' Then the class hums the music till the end.

Boxes, boxes, boxes! Mom wishes for a rest, but the boxes must go in the shed. Mom drags one box. I drag two. Then the dog dashes in. It grabs a stick from a box and rushes off! 'Drop it!' The dog just dashes past the benches. It wishes for a game of fetch. So Mom tosses the stick, and the dog fetches it. Rest, then boxes! Mom smiles and fills two dishes — one for me, one for the dog.

We camped at the lake. Dad packed the tent. I helped — well, I helped a bit. Then we fished. And fished. And fished. Not a fish. 'One last cast,' said Dad. A tug! A big tug! 'A fish!' I shouted. I held on, and Dad helped, and we landed it: a big, big fish! Dad smiled. We baked the fish on the grill and munched it up. Then we rested in the tent as the sun set. Best trip yet!

Sam is fishing at the pond. The frog is jumping on the logs. Plop! The dog is dashing and splashing. 'Stop splashing!' said Sam. 'The fish!' But the frog kept jumping, and the dog kept splashing, and the fish swam off. Sam sat. And sat. We watch him fishing. At sunset — a tug! Sam lands a fish at last, and he is glad. The frog jumps in with a plop. The dog is resting on the sand. And Sam? Sam is singing.

Ben has a robot. It can go so fast! It buzzes and hums and zips. 'Race to the sofa!' The robot wins. 'Race to the bed!' The robot wins. Ben huffs. 'You win so much!' 'I am a robot,' said the robot. So Ben made a plan. 'Race up the steps!' The robot can not go up steps! Ben wins at last. 'You win, Ben,' said the robot. So they call it even. Then Ben must catch the robot for bed. What a fun robot!

Fudge sits at the edge of the bridge. Fudge will not budge. 'Nudge him,' said Mom. Del gives Fudge a nudge. Fudge just sits. 'A snack?' Fudge sniffs. Fudge sits. 'A hug?' Fudge sits. Del slumps at the edge. Then a kind child strolls up with a big snack. Fudge stands! Fudge trots! Fudge is off the bridge at once! 'What a dog,' said Del with a grin. 'A snack from a kind child wins.'

'Gold!' said Rose. 'The old map tells of gold in the mud flats.' So we dig. It is cold, and the mud is wet. 'Be kind and hold my hand,' I tell Rose — the mud grips and pulls. We dig till the sun is up. Clunk! A box! We try to lift it. In the box: the old gold! We both hold it up in the sun. I am told it is mine, but Rose gets the small gold cup, and I get the rest. Rich at last — and cold, and wet, and glad!

My kite can fly! Well... it can try. I fly it by the pond. It flops. 'Do not cry,' said Dad. 'Ask why.' Why? No wind! So we sit by the pond. We sit... and sit... At last — wind! I run fast and let the line go long. Up! Up it goes! My kite is a shy dot in the sun. 'Why did it fly?' said Dad. 'Wind!' said I. Dad is happy, and so am I.

Sam is happy. The puppy is funny. The sky is sunny. A picnic! Mom set up jelly and buns. The silly puppy got jelly on its fuzzy chin — and then on my lap, and then on Sam! 'Bad puppy!' But no one is mad — it is just funny. We had such fun. Then candy at school as well. What a lucky bunch we are!

A little apple, a bottle of milk, and a blink match on the rug — what a plan! Sam and I sat still. Do not blink... do not blink... I blinked! Sam got the win — but just by a little. Gran came to see, and she clapped. Then we giggled and jumped in a puddle by the gate. Gran is gentle: she patted my hand. 'A blink match, a puddle and a giggle,' said Gran. 'What a simple, happy time!' Then a snuggle on the rug, a little apple, a bottle of milk — and bed.

The farm is dark. The car naps in the yard. But the dog? The dog is up! It darts in the yard. It barks at the stars. It digs by the barn. Dig, dig, dig! What is it? A bone! The dog grips the bone hard. But hark — Mom calls from the barn. The dog must turn back. It trots to the barn in the dark, bone and all. And then the dog naps — not in the barn. In the car!

A bird sits on the birch and chirps. Burt turns. 'A bird!' The bird twirls, darts to the fern, and chirps on. Burt gets a crust and tosses it. The bird pecks the crust. Chirp! It chirps for one more. Burt tosses one more. 'That is hard work,' said Burt with a smirk, 'but a bird is a bird.' The bird whirls up, chirps a last chirp — thanks, Burt! — and whirls off. Burt waves. 'Turn up next time, bird!'

Rain. Rain all week. We keep inside and read. We sit and wait. We read and dream. We see the rain each day. We even see rain at night! 'Will it ever end?' Then — at last — a beam! The sun beams and beams. We run to the green trees. We leap in the wet grass. The clean street steams in the heat. The best week? This week — rain, dreams and all!

We look up at the moon. It is cool and good. Soon a fox trots into the moonlight! The fox took its food up the road. We keep still. We look and look. The fox looks back at us... then zooms off into the gloom. A hoot drifts from a tree near us. Hoot, hoot! 'Time to go in,' said Mom. But it is so good to sit in the cool night — the moon, the fox and the hoots.

We went out and about. Dark clouds. A loud wind all around us. Then — crack! A storm found us! We shout and turn back fast. We count the thunder as we run. BOOM! How loud it is! We pound down the path and burst inside, wet and dripping. 'I know that sound,' said Dad with a grin. 'That was thunder. Now, who is up for hot food?'

Sam had a big dog. The dog ran to see a fox! The fox sat up on a big rock. She did not run. She sat. The dog can not get up the rock. It yaps and yaps. Sam had to run to get his dog. The fox hid in a log and sat snug in it. At last Sam got his dog. The dog just naps in the sun. And the fox naps in the log.

A fat frog sat on a wet log. It looked at the pond and saw six bugs. Yum! The frog did a big jump — and a big flop! The bugs left fast. The frog could not get up on the log. It swam to a flat stump and sat. The wind was soft. The pond was flat. At sunset the frog did a last big jump — and got up! Not a bug in the pond. But what a jump!

My dog ran down to the pond. Splash? He can see a big fish with sharp fins! The dog did not jump in. Not this dog! He ran back up the path fast, with wet legs and a yip. I got him a snack and a pat. 'It is just a fish,' I tell him. Then he was glad. He ran back to the pond with me — but he sat well back from the bank. We had fun in the sun till it got dim.

The hens sat in the sun. Six big bugs ran up the wall. The hens did not see them — but the cat did! The cat had a long look. It could not get them. The wall is tall, and the cat is not. The cat sat still. Still... still... the bugs went zigzag up to the top! The two bugs ran off to play. The cat quit. It had a sip of water and a long nap in the sun. And the hens? The hens just sat in the sun.

My best friend had a birthday party. We made a big cake with green frosting — well, Mom made it. We helped. I could not wait to eat it. We all sang, and my friend made a wish. 'What did you wish for?' 'I can not say — or it will not come true!' My friend thought it was the best cake we had made. We each had two big slices. Then we ran outside to play games in the backyard. At the end we took a break, and I heard soft music from the porch. Such a happy day! I hope my party will be just as good.
